evidence.note: Verified in bash that `set -euo pipefail; ! true; echo alive` still prints alive: POSIX/bash ignore -e for a pipeline preceded by `!`, so the removed `! git check-ignore -q ...` assertions never failed the script. The replacement `cmd && exit 1` is the correct idiom (verified `true && exit 1` exits 1, `false && exit 1` continues).

All ten converted negative assertions are top-level statements (not inside functions or subshells), so `exit 1` terminates the test script as intended. Repo-wide grep for `^[[:space:]]*![[:space:]]` under tests/ returns zero hits, so the vacuous-assertion fix was applied consistently rather than partially.
